keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Naqada I "(about 3900-3650 BC)" and Naqada II "(about 3650-3300 BC)" in Upper Egypt; infobox "c. 4000-3000 BC". The page says Naqada II is "represented throughout Egypt", but the Maadi page keeps Lower Egypt Maadian "until Naqada IIc/d" and "by the end of Naqada II circa 3200 BCE", so the north is added only in 3200 BCE. The Nile clip of the Upper Egypt region is this dossier's; Naqada I "traded with Nubia to the south, the oases of the western desert to the west", which is trade, not drawn. No area figure to compare.

certainty.note: An archaeological culture confined to the Nile valley: the desert edge is sharp by nature, the southern limit toward Nubia and the northern limit against the Maadian are soft.

notes: Culture dossier. The culture outlives the group's 3400 BCE horizon to Cliopatria's Early Dynastic row in 3000 BCE so that Egypt is never blank. Disagreements: start 4000 BC (infobox) vs 3800-3700 BC (Oxford study); end 2900 (Naqada III), 3100 (Oxford) or 3000 (Cliopatria row); Naqada II "throughout Egypt" (Naqada page) vs the Maadian Delta to c. 3200 BCE (Maadi page). Lower Nubia (Qustul, the A-Group) is not on the pages and is not drawn. Gazetteer: Naqada, Nekhen/Hierakonpolis, Abydos, Buto are not places; the Upper Egypt region clipped to a 40 km Nile band and the Lower Egypt and Fayyum regions stand in.
